content:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY — GARRETT REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER
(Outside hospital records, received at University Medical Center 4/30/2027)

Patient: Whitlock, Sarah L, 50F
Admission date: 4/28/2027 (via Garrett Regional ED)
Discharge date: 4/30/2027
Attending: Dr. Lena Park (Hospital Medicine); ICU care Dr. R. Sandoval (Critical Care)

ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to acute bilateral pulmonary edema — resolved with diuresis.
2. Decompensated alcohol-related cirrhosis with diuretic-refractory ascites and recurrent right hepatic hydrothorax (followed at University Hepatology; transplant evaluation in progress).
3. Hepatic encephalopathy, controlled on lactulose/rifaximin.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 50F with decompensated cirrhosis who has been receiving weekly therapeutic thoracentesis and paracentesis at Garrett Regional Radiology for several weeks. On the morning of 4/28 she had her scheduled drainage session at that facility, with the facility's usual peri-procedural protocol (4 units of fresh frozen plasma plus albumin for INR 2.0). That evening she developed rapidly progressive shortness of breath and was brought to our ED. On arrival: afebrile, BP 104/65, HR 112, RR 30, SpO2 82% on room air, using accessory muscles and fatigued.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
- Portable chest X-ray showed diffuse BILATERAL pulmonary edema, distinct from her known isolated right-sided effusion. She was intubated for hypoxemic respiratory failure and admitted to the ICU.
- Labs on arrival: BNP markedly elevated (920 pg/mL); troponin negative; WBC normal; liver indices near her chronic baseline (see attached results). Bedside transthoracic echocardiogram: preserved EF (~60%), no valvular or regional wall-motion abnormality, normal right ventricle.
- Treated with IV furosemide with brisk diuresis and rapid improvement in oxygenation.
- Extubated 4/29. Weaned to nasal cannula and then room air.
- Discharged home 4/30 at her respiratory baseline.

PROCEDURES: Endotracheal intubation (4/28); extubation (4/29).

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE: Stable, room air, alert and oriented, ambulating.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: Home regimen unchanged — spironolactone 50 mg daily, furosemide 20 mg daily, lactulose three times daily, rifaximin 550 mg three times daily, thiamine, folate.

FOLLOW-UP / INSTRUCTIONS:
- Follow up with her hepatologist, Dr. Hale, at University Hepatology this week; records faxed.
- She intends to continue her weekly drainage sessions at Garrett Regional Radiology under the facility's existing protocol unless her University team advises otherwise.
- Return for any recurrence of shortness of breath.
attestation: Electronically signed by Dr. Lena Park, MD (Hospital Medicine, Garrett Regional Medical Center). 4/30/2027. Outside records received by University Medical Center 4/30/2027.
